subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Anthropic & OpenModel - NexaCare
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nexacarehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Anthropic & OpenModel - NexaCare

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. I captured the main points below; please reply with any corrections.

Attendees:
- Samantha Li (NexaCare)
- Tom Ellis (NexaCare)
- Aditya Rao (Redwood)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood, solutions)

Pain points / current constraints:
- Latency spikes on peak loads causing poor UX for clinicians (p95 sometimes > 2s).
- High per-request cost with current vendor when using long-context notes.
- Lack of clear model versioning and audit trails for clinical prompts.
- Concern about multi-region failover and data residency for PHI.

Goals / decision criteria:
1) Latency: consistent p95 under 350ms for summary calls (typical prompt lengths).
2) Cost: target 30% reduction in token cost vs current provider on our workload.
3) Reliability & fallbacks: multi-region routing + graceful degradation to smaller model variants.
4) Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence, support for customer-managed KMS, and VPC option.
5) Observability: token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing for audit.

Competitive context discussed:
- NexaCare will run a 2-week bake-off comparing Redwood, Anthropic, and OpenModel's hosted endpoint.
- Tests will include: (a) throughput/latency under synthetic load, (b) cost-per-session on a representative note set, (c) quality blind evals on 50 sample records, (d) failover behavior across regions.

Open questions / assumptions:
- Do you have a baseline token-cost extract from your current vendor we can use?
- Are all test records de-identified, or will any PHI remain in the POC dataset? (important for infra choices)
- Preferred time window for running load tests (US business hours or overnight)?

Next steps / owners:
- Aditya: send bake-off plan + sample workload template by Mon (attached). (Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf)
- Samantha: share current vendor cost report + confirm dataset de-id status by Tue.
- Marissa: coordinate POC infra (dedicated test pool) and prepare runbook.
- Schedule: aim to start tests week of Oct 12, 2026.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a formal POC plan and a short runbook so your infra team can scope the Dedicated/vpc needs.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-summary.pdf (application/pdf, 124 KB)

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nexacarehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nexacarehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Anthropic & OpenModel - NexaCare

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap — this looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: we can provide a de-identified set of ~200 notes for quality evals. For load/cost tests we can share a synthetic generator that matches token distributions. No PHI in POC dataset.
2) Cost baseline: attached a 30-day summary export from our current vendor (see notes column).
3) Timing: overnight runs are preferable for load tests (02:00–06:00 PT) to avoid clinician impact.

Decision weighting: our final decision will prioritize (1) consistent latency (40%), (2) cost (30%), (3) integration & auditability (20%), (4) vendor support & roadmap (10%).

Open question for Redwood: can you support a customer-managed KMS for key storage during the POC, or will we be using Redwood-managed keys initially? If customer-managed is not possible for the POC, we need an architectural explanation for how keys and logs are isolated.

Thanks — I’ve attached the vendor cost export (vendor-cost-export.csv).

—Samantha
Director, Platform Integrations
NexaCare

Attachment: vendor-cost-export.csv (text/csv, 18 KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nexacarehealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nexacarehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Anthropic & OpenModel - NexaCare

Great — thanks for the attachments and the decision weighting, that helps a lot. Quick answers and next steps: 

- KMS: We can support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For the hosted POC we typically use Redwood-managed keys but can enable a customer-managed KMS in your dedicated test VPC if you prefer; Marissa will include the steps in the runbook.
- Overnight window works — we’ll schedule load profiles for 02:00–06:00 PT.
- I’m attaching the formal POC plan and a proposed list of tests (nexacare-poc-plan.xlsx). The plan includes the latency and cost measurement scripts, the blind-eval protocol, and the failover checklist.

Proposed schedule:
- Oct 6: infra prep & access credentials exchanged
- Oct 12–13: run bake-off (load + cost tests)
- Oct 14–15: blind quality evals and review
- Oct 19: vendor results meeting & decision checkpoint

Action items:
- Aditya: provision test endpoints (Redwood hosted + dedicated test pool) and share credentials to your infra team by Oct 6.
- Marissa: follow up with a runbook and KMS steps (will loop infra).
- Samantha: confirm dataset delivery and time window by Oct 5.

If that all looks good I’ll open a HubSpot deal note and share the Drive folder with the runbook link.

Best,
Aditya

Attachment: nexacare-poc-plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 42 KB)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nexacarehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@nexacarehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Anthropic & OpenModel - NexaCare

Thanks Aditya — schedule looks good. We’ll aim to deliver the de-id dataset and the cost report by EOD Oct 5. 

One quick ask: during the overnight load tests can you expose per-request tracing so we can correlate latency spikes to request size? That will be helpful for our SREs.

—Tom
Sr. Engineering Manager
NexaCare
